<findings>
<finding task="3"><quote>R1.3 **`compatibility`.** When present, a string of 1–500 characters after stripping.</quote><plan>R1.3: `compatibility` is "a string of 1–500 UTF-8 bytes after stripping".</plan><fix>Count characters, not bytes, as the spec does. In Global Constraints, restore the verbatim quote "a string of 1–500 characters after stripping". In Task 3, set `COMPATIBILITY_CAP = 500` characters and test `1 <= len(compat.strip()) <= COMPATIBILITY_CAP`. Change the error text to `compatibility must be a string of 1-500 characters`. Rename the test to `test_compatibility_must_be_a_string_of_1_to_500_characters`, and add one case with a 500-character multibyte value that must pass.</fix></finding>
<finding task="3"><quote>**State test changes as +N deltas** against the suite, never absolute totals.</quote><plan>Expected: `4 failed, 41 passed`, the four new tests.</plan><fix>Write every expected pytest result as a delta against the suite's pre-task result. For example, Step 2 becomes "Expected: +4 failed (the four new tests), the rest unchanged" and Step 6 becomes "+4 passed". Apply the same change to the absolute summaries in Tasks 4–12, the "(22, 9, 27, 268, …)" suite counts in Task 10 Step 6, and the `37/37` totals in Task 15.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>Each new lint rule has a test that failed before its implementation and passes after.</quote><plan>## Global Constraints</plan><fix>Add the required `## Review Focus` section between Global Constraints and Decisions. It lists the five uncovered inputs most likely to bite a user, each with a test in the task whose code would fail:
(1) a SKILL.md with CRLF line endings, where `FRONTMATTER_RE` silently skips the body warning (Task 6);
(2) an invocation written with `python3.13` or `python -u`, which the invocation lint misses (Task 11);
(3) a `__main__` guard written as `if "__main__" == __name__:` or indented in a block (Task 10);
(4) a `compatibility` value whose multibyte characters push it past 500 bytes but not 500 characters (Task 3);
(5) a `metadata: null` or empty mapping (Task 3).
Each test asserts the user-visible lint output.</fix></finding>

    '''Every SKILL.md names its license (portability R1.4: repo policy, beyond
    the spec), so a single-skill install still says how the skill is licensed.'''
    lic = fm.get('license')
    if isinstance(lic, str) and lic.strip():

Replace each body with its signature, its pinned constants, and its test. Keep code only where the tests leave a choice, such as the PEP 723 regex and the optional-import walk, and for exact copy the spec fixes.</fix></finding>
